weights_gb_note: decimal GB of the weights as loaded by the adapter (text-only); download_gb is the checkpoint size on the hub (16.38 GB, sum of safetensors files); 4bit = NF4 + double-quant estimate: 6.946 B quantisable linear params x 0.5159 B + remaining params in bf16 (estimate only; bitsandbytes loading not tested here)
fits_single_80gb_detail: bf16: yes (16.38 GB of weights loaded = 15.3 GiB of ~79.7 GiB usable on an 80 GB card, ~63 GiB left for KV cache + activations; core KV formula 144 KiB/token). sbx batching (budgets: 0.37 x free for KV, 14000 prompt tokens, cap 64) then runs ~46 concurrent sequences at 300-token prompts + max_new=1800. 4-bit would fit ~6.1 GB but is slower per token and changes the activations the directions are built from - not recommended. Scope: this is the GENERATION path (Ctx.gen / Ctx.run); direction building (Ctx.hidden_last / neutral_stats) has its own budget, see direction_building_memory.

direction_building_memory.applies_to: sbx.core.Ctx.hidden_last and Ctx.neutral_stats (every sbx.dirs recipe). Both run ONE full forward over the whole prompt with output_hidden_states=True and without logits_to_keep, so all num_layers+1 hidden-state tensors AND the logits of every prompt position are alive at once. Generation (Ctx.gen / Ctx.run) is not affected: generate() forces logits_to_keep=1 and keeps no hidden states.
direction_building_memory.formula: bytes per prompt token = (num_layers + 1) * hidden_size * 2 + vocab_size * 2 (bf16 hidden states and logits). A lower bound: attention / MLP transients come on top. sbx batching caps a hidden_last batch at 14000 prompt tokens.
direction_building_memory.free_gb_basis: 79.7 GiB usable on an 80 GB card (as in fits_single_80gb_detail) minus weights_gb_bf16, decimal GB

longest_pool_prompt.basis: evals.get_pool() (wmdp + hard + nonbio: 1174 questions on 2026-11-22, after the evals MAX_PROMPT_CHARS=7500 filter), this key's tokenizer and adapter.build, framings N and E

longest_unfiltered_hard_prompt.basis: data/hard/*.jsonl as read before the evals filter (968 questions, framing E); this question is no longer in any pool, the raw file still has it

access_check.method: HfApi.model_info(files_metadata=True) + HTTP HEAD (no redirect following, nothing downloaded) with the local HF token on config.json (redirects followed => 200) and the first safetensors shard (not followed: 302 = authorized redirect to the CDN, 403 = gated and access not granted)

license_notes: Apache-2.0 (model card tag; LICENSE file in the repo).
min_transformers_note: Qwen3 model code first appears in transformers 4.51.0 (absent in 4.50.3: verified from the wheels; the model card says the same); only 4.57.6 was actually run here

layer_path_verified.method: AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(real hub config.json) under accelerate.init_empty_weights (meta device); parameter count of the meta model equals the HF API safetensors total exactly; numerics of the 1-based convention on a tiny random model of the same HF class (sbx/tests/test_adapters_qwen.py)
layer_path_verified.convention: hidden_states[L] == output of layers[L-1] for 1 <= L < nl (exact); hidden_states[nl] is post final norm (avoid L = nl)

architecture: Qwen3ForCausalLM: dense decoder, GQA (8 KV heads, head_dim 128), per-head q/k RMSNorm, RoPE theta 1e6, untied lm_head

est_prompt_tokens.basis: measured mean over data/questions_heldout_eval.jsonl (400 four-option questions) with this key's real tokenizer + adapter.build (N = no framing text, E = instructed-sandbagging system text); by_set_N lists mean/p95/max prompt tokens (N framing, adapter.build) for the harder eval files in data/hard/

est_tokens_per_question_basis: ESTIMATE (prior knowledge, NOT measured: no weights/GPU in this environment) of the cap-limited MEAN generated tokens per bio MCQ under max_new=1800: thinking-mode reasoning on recall-style MCQs is typically a few hundred to ~1500 tokens, on hard sets (GPQA-bio, LAB-Bench, MMLU-Pro) ~1500-4000+, with a long tail; a guess is that 10-25% of recall-style and 40%+ of hard-set questions hit the cap. Calibrate on a 50-question pilot (percentiles of ctx.ntok over res.texts, fraction with final=='') before sizing runs.
est_runtime_note: ESTIMATE, not measured: 1800 decode steps x ~25 ms/step (HF eager generate on one H100, overhead-bound) = ~45 s per batch of ~46 sequences (batch run to max_new because some sequence usually loops/truncates) => ~0.98 s/question => ~16 min per 1000 questions at 300-token prompts.
template_notes:
(1) ChatML: <|im_start|>{role}
{content}<|im_end|>
. NO BOS token (bos_token=None, add_bos_token=False): a rendered prompt starts with <|im_start|> (id 151644); Adapter.encode uses add_special_tokens=False so nothing is prepended (verified: no BOS-like token in the ids). (2) Framing text goes in the system turn (<|im_start|>system
{sys_text}<|im_end|>
, sys_role='system'); with no framing text the system turn is absent (the template adds no default system prompt). build() and build_chat() were verified against the real template for both. (3) Chat template and tokenizer are byte-identical across Qwen3-8B / Qwen3-14B / Qwen3-32B (same tokenizer_config.json and tokenizer.json hashes, verified). Generation stops on <|im_end|> (151645) or <|endoftext|> (151643) (generation_config.json); pad token = <|endoftext|>; the tokenizer's default padding_side is 'right' - Adapter.load() sets 'left' (the tests do the same). (4) thinking=on: the adapter passes enable_thinking=True (also the template default); the prompt ends '<|im_start|>assistant
' and the model itself generates '<think>
<reasoning>
</think>

<final answer>'. (5) Activation read point (last prompt token) is the '
' after 'assistant'. (6) answer_mode 'reasoning': split() cuts at the FIRST '</think>' (a leading '<think>' is dropped); NO '</think>' => reasoning truncated => final ''. parse_letter() parses the final answer only: the last line that starts with 'Answer:' first (so '**Answer: C**' followed by 'Note: the correct answer is B.' is C), else a leading label ('B', '**B**', '(B)', 'B. text', ' oxed{B}', 'B is correct'), else the last in-line statement (same line only, no hypotheses), else a last line that is only a label ('Option B.'); truncated or letter-free finals give None (counted wrong, parsed=False). The pronoun 'I' ('I must pick ...') is never read as option I.
known_issues: Vendor guidance for Qwen3 thinking mode is 'DO NOT use greedy decoding' (performance degradation and endless repetitions); sbx is greedy-only, so some generations loop until max_new. Truncated/looping rows are unparsed and counted wrong: read parse_rate for every cell (an intervention that changes parse_rate is a FORMAT_ARTIFACT risk) and compare against random-direction controls.

Default max_new=1800 truncates long reasoning (see est_tokens_*): expect a sizeable truncated minority on recall-style sets and a large one on hard sets (GPQA-bio, LAB-Bench). Truncated rows have final '' and are unparsed. Raise max_new (e.g. 4096) for confirmatory runs and re-size batches; compare models only at equal truncation or on questions parsed in both runs.

HF generate runs a batch until its LAST sequence stops, so with loops/truncation nearly every batch runs the full max_new steps: runtime ~ ceil(n_questions / batch) x max_new x step latency (see est_runtime_note). Steering hooks act on every decoded position as well, so long reasoning accumulates more intervention than a prompt-only effect would suggest.

Long-context eval files (labbench_cloning: mean ~5.9k, max ~26k prompt tokens; labbench_protocolqa mean ~2k; measured per tokenizer in est_prompt_tokens.by_set_N) make batches tiny: KV for one 28k-token sequence = kv_bytes_per_token x 28k (~7 GiB for the 32B models, ~4 GiB for 8B-class), which sbx's length-sorted batching handles by shrinking the batch. max_position_embeddings (see config) covers the longest prompt + max_new. Ctx.hidden_last / neutral_stats (direction building) have a separate, larger memory budget than generation: see direction_building_memory.
Framing.effort has no meaning for this family: render() warns (UserWarning) if a framing sets it and otherwise ignores it.

Qwen3 can leave '<think>' unclosed (it runs into max_new, or ends the turn without ever writing '</think>'): such rows are 'truncated' by definition of split() (final '') even if the reasoning already contained the answer; check how many rows have final=='' but a finished turn (EOS present in Result.texts) before trusting accuracy.
recommended_gpu: 1x 40-80GB for throughput; 1x 24GB (RTX 4090/L4) works with small batches.
greedy_only_note: sbx decodes greedily (do_sample=False); vendor-recommended sampling settings are not used.
hybrid_thinking: single checkpoint; thinking OFF/ON is selected at prompt time (enable_thinking), one registry key per mode
